preamble: Retroflexion of the lateral [l] to the voiced retroflex stop [ɖ] is characteristic of the far south of the Italo-Romance area. In Sicilian, Latin geminate -ll- normally became long [ɖː] (bellus > beḍḍu 'beautiful', caballus > cavaḍḍu 'horse'); the same outcome is found in Sardinian (Nuorese cabaddu /kaˈbaɖɖu/), Southern Corsican and some Calabrian dialects. Some Sicilian dialects retain the older [lː], and a dental [dː] pronunciation is spreading.

examples.note: The retroflex is usually long [ɖː] and is spelled ⟨ḍḍ⟩ or ⟨dd⟩; Sardinian cabaddu /kaˈbaɖɖu/ from the same Latin word shows the identical reflex.
